question: How is the yoginī named Icchā transmitted by the siddhas up to the limit of māyā?
premises: A yoginī named Icchā is identified.
The siddhas are involved in transmission.
The transmission reaches up to māyā by supreme will.
inference: The yoginī Icchā is transmitted by the siddhas up to the limit of māyā through supreme will.
uncertainties: The exact syntactic relation of māyāntaṃ to the rest of the verse is unclear.
plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā was transmitted by the siddhas, up to the limit of māyā, by supreme will.
